newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end lower amid setback for Vale sale.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end lower amid setback for Vale sale.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed slightly down in a slow session despite high volume, amid worries over congressional opposition to the privatization of mining giant Vale do Rio Doce, brokers said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 49 most traded shares fell 157 points, or 0.24 percent, to 65,413 points. Volume was high at 487.8 million reais ($471.07 million).
Former presidents Jose Sarney and Itamar Franco have joined forces in opposing Vale's selloff, scheduled to begin in February next year.
Worries mounted after newspapers reported Jose Sarney, Senate's president, suggested he might trade his opposition to presidential re-election for more Senate oversight of the Vale sale.
Vale preferred shares fell over one percent earlier following the news but recouped some of its losses to end slightly down at 21.20 reais.
"Vale will be a big privatization and any opposition to the selloff is not welcome," said a senior trader.
Benchmark Telebras preferred closed flat at 76.90 reais.
The company's common stock ended off 0.15 percent at 64.70 reais.
Among other blue-chips, state oil firm Petrobras holding company Eletrobras gained 0.29 percent to 339 reais.
Shares of Rio de Janeiro power utility Cerj jumped 4.08 percent to 0.51 reais following the company's privatization auction earlier today in the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange (BVRJ).
The firm was auctioned off to a consortium led by Chile's Chilectra, which acquired a 70.2 percent stake for 605.3 million reais.

Traders also noted Sao Paulo state bank Banespa preferred continued its uptrend today on optimism over an agreement between the state and federal governments on a restructuring plan for Sao Paulo's debt with Banespa, expected to be announced soon.
Analysts said the market is likely to remain soft Thursday unless positive market-moving news comes out.
